source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The three boards are chained: power board → main board → sensor board. The main board is in the middle, so power enters from the power board (J\_PWR\_PWR) and the main board uses it locally AND forwards it to the sensor board (J\_SENSOR\_PWR). Think of it like a power strip — power comes in one cable, and the main board distributes it both to its own components and passes it along to the sensor board via a second cable.
The INA219 sits in-series on the 3.3V rail right after the Schottky diodes — so it measures the total 3.3V current for everything downstream: the ESP32 itself, plus whatever the sensor board draws, all in one reading.

value_updates.board_power_topology: power board → main board → sensor board

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
For the sensor board, it has two input connectors coming from the main board — one 4-pin JST-PH 2.0mm for power (5V, GND, 3V3, GND) and one 6-pin JST-GH 1.25mm for signals (SDA0, SCL0, SDA1, SCL1, UART TX, UART RX).
Then it has output connectors going to each sensor module:

\- SCD41 — 4-pin JST-GH (3V3/GND/SDA0/SCL0)
\- BME280 — 4-pin JST-GH
\- ENS160 — 4-pin JST-GH
\- SPS30 — 5-pin JST-ZH 1.5mm (5V, SDA0, SCL0, SEL→GND, GND) — different connector type, matches SPS30 cable
\- ZE08-CH2O — 7-pin JST-GH (matches supplied cable)
\- I2C display — 4-pin JST-GH (3V3/GND/SDA1/SCL1)
\- One spare I2C0 port — 4-pin JST-GH
\- One spare I2C1 port — 4-pin JST-GH

So 10 connectors total. Full pinouts are in the sensor board doc.
